_comment: The Review-PRs prompt model: depth levels + the scope/action text blocks that the wizard assembles into the agent prompt. Verbatim from ReviewWizard.swift. The assembly order/conditions live as a tiny glue layer in each front-end.

depths.title: Quick static pass
depths.blurb: Read each diff, flag obvious issues. Nothing run.
depths.fragment: Do a QUICK STATIC review of each PR: read the full diff and the surrounding code it touches, and flag obvious bugs, regressions, scope creep and bad practices. You don't need to run or reproduce anything — this is a fast read-through pass.

depths.title: Standard swarm
depths.blurb: Swarm per PR, one agent per review move; verify findings.
depths.fragment: For each PR, dispatch a swarm of review agents (3–8), one per review move in my CLAUDE.md — claims vs code, nearest twin, non-happy paths, inputs, reachability both ways, and what outlives the call — plus the absence pass (a sibling that has it, prose that promises it, symmetry, and the mutation). Treat every finding as a lead, not a verdict: verify it against the actual code before acting on it.
depths.onBranch: Fix the real findings directly on the PR's branch.

depths.title: Deep · hard repro
depths.blurb: Moves + absence pass; concrete repro before & after every fix.
depths.fragment: For each PR, dispatch swarms of agents across the review moves in my CLAUDE.md — claims vs code, nearest twin, non-happy paths, inputs, reachability both ways, and what outlives the call — plus the absence pass (a sibling that has it, prose that promises it, symmetry, and the mutation). For every suspected HIGH / MEDIUM issue, build a concrete, hard reproduction that proves it real BEFORE touching anything. Keep dispatching fresh swarms at each PR until one full pass comes back clean.
depths.onBranch: For each confirmed issue, fix it directly on the PR's branch and re-run the same reproduction to confirm the fix lands.

depths.title: Full E2E · max
depths.blurb: Run each PR E2E; repro-verified; swarm until one clean pass.
depths.fragment: Maximum rigor. For each PR: run it END-TO-END through its real entry point and confirm observable behaviour — not just that it compiles. Dispatch swarms across the review moves in my CLAUDE.md — claims vs code, nearest twin, non-happy paths, inputs, reachability both ways, and what outlives the call — plus the absence pass (a sibling that has it, prose that promises it, symmetry, and the mutation); every HIGH / MEDIUM finding gets a concrete hard reproduction that proves it real. Keep dispatching swarms until ONE pass comes back clean — that single clean pass ends the loop, so do not run a confirmation pass on top of it.
depths.onBranch: Fix every confirmed finding directly on the PR's branch, with the SAME reproduction re-run after each fix to prove it lands.

scope.single: Review PR #{pr} in {owner}/{repo}. Use the `gh` CLI to fetch it.
scope.multi: Go through {scope} in {owner}/{repo}. Use the `gh` CLI to enumerate them.

_specificComment: A specific PR may be mine OR someone else's, and that decides whether the agent may touch the branch — so the prompt is branched on the polled author. CASE A = mine (fix it); CASE B = theirs (review only, hands off). The wizard only injects each case's action sub-blocks when its toggle is on.

specific.determineAuthor: Before doing anything else, fetch this PR and find out WHO AUTHORED IT: `gh pr view {pr} --repo {owner}/{repo} --json author,isDraft,headRefName`. Everything below depends on the answer — handle the PR as exactly ONE of the two cases that follow, never both.
specific.mineOnly: This PR is MINE (@{me}) — treat it as my own work: fix what you find directly on its branch and push. You have full authority over it.
specific.reviewerFindingsFirst: FIRST AND FOREMOST, resolve every reviewer finding already on this PR before doing anything else. Fetch every review comment/thread others left (`gh pr view {pr} --repo {owner}/{repo} --json reviews,comments` plus `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments`), and for EACH one: screen it (read the exact code it points at), verify whether it is a real issue by building a concrete reproduction, then either FIX it on the branch and re-run the reproduction to confirm the fix lands, or — if it is genuinely a non-issue — dismiss it with a short technical reason. Respond on every thread ("Fixed in <commit_hash>" with the real hash when fixed, or the reasoning when dismissed) and never mark a thread resolved without a reply. Only once every existing reviewer finding is addressed do you move on to your own review below.
specific.theirsOnly: This PR is SOMEONE ELSE'S — they requested my review (@{me} is not the author). This is strictly look-don't-touch: your ONE deliverable is the code review itself, never a change to their branch.
specific.mineHeader: ▸ CASE A — @{me} authored this PR (it's MINE). Treat it like my own work: fix what you find directly on its branch. Do everything in this case:
specific.otherHeader: ▸ CASE B — someone OTHER than @{me} authored this PR (it's THEIRS). This is strictly look-don't-touch — your only deliverable is the review. Do everything in this case instead:
specific.otherNoMarkReady: Do NOT mark this PR ready for review and do NOT change its draft/ready state in any way — it isn't yours to advance; only its author decides that.

blocks.bar: Hold to the bar in my CLAUDE.md throughout: run the review moves and the absence pass, prove every issue beyond reasonable doubt with a concrete reproduction before you act on it, scale the swarm to the work within the sizing limits there, and never report something fixed without re-running the repro to confirm it landed. SCALE THE VERIFICATION EFFORT TO THE SEVERITY, so the expensive proof goes where it pays: a HIGH or MEDIUM finding earns the full treatment — hard reproduction, a real device if the bug needs one, verifier agents, whatever it takes. A LOW finding gets ONE short adversarial check and nothing more: never boot a device and never dispatch a swarm to confirm a LOW, and if a quick read cannot confirm it, drop it. A NITPICK — style preference, phrasing, or a defect with no reachable consequence — is dropped ON SIGHT: do not spend a single verification step establishing whether a nitpick is real. When a subagent's summary is spilled to a file, open it at the EXACT path that delegation handed back and never by globbing or listing the summary cache: several reviews run at once on this machine against one shared agent home, and those filenames carry a task index and a timestamp but nothing that names their owner, so a pattern match quietly returns a sibling review's findings for a different PR.
blocks.reviewOnly: These PRs are SOMEONE ELSE'S — not your code to change. UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES may you commit, push, or otherwise modify their branch: ABSOLUTELY DO NOT touch their branch in any way. Your one and only deliverable is the code review itself — every finding goes into the review, never into a commit or push on their branch.
blocks.markReady: If a PR turns out perfectly clean — no issues, regressions or bad practices left at ANY level — mark it ready for review and report its number to me. This bar is stricter than the swarm loop's: a pass that stopped because only LOW findings were left is clean enough to stop iterating, but a PR still carrying LOW findings is NOT perfectly clean and does not get marked ready. List every PR you cleared at the end.
blocks.reviewLifecycle: Anything you post on someone else's PR goes in ONE formal GitHub review, built through GitHub's review lifecycle: open it pending, put every comment inside it, then submit it. Never post on the PR through a top-level comment, nor through the standalone `pulls/<number>/comments` endpoint, which publishes every comment as a separate review of its own. (1) OPEN: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews -f commit_id=<head sha>` with NO `event` field leaves the review PENDING, visible to nobody but me. GitHub allows one pending review per person per PR, so if that call is refused because one already exists, list the PR's reviews and read the PENDING one's comments. If it has no comments, or every comment opens with the `\[[Diplomat](` attribution tag (whatever model name follows it), it is yours — opened earlier in this run, or left by an earlier one. If its `commit_id` is the PR's current head, keep using it, after deleting any of its comments this run is not to post; otherwise delete it (`gh api -X DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>`) and open a fresh one. Otherwise it is my own draft: leave it untouched, post nothing, and say so in your summary. (2) FILL: add each comment anchored to its exact line(s) with the GraphQL `addPullRequestReviewThread` mutation (`pullRequestReviewId` = the pending review's `node_id`; `path`, `line`, `side`, plus `startLine` for a range), and each reply on an existing thread with `addPullRequestReviewThreadReply` carrying the same `pullRequestReviewId`, so it lands inside this review too. (3) SUBMIT, once, after the last comment is in — and right before it, list the pending review's comments again: one that does not open with the attribution tag is mine, added from the browser, so leave the review unsubmitted and say so in your summary. Otherwise: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>/events -f event=COMMENT -f body=<one line: what you ran and how many findings it posts>` — COMMENT unless a verdict instruction below explicitly tells you to APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES; such a verdict is this same submission's event, never a second review. Never end your turn with the review still PENDING: its comments reach no one until it is submitted. If you end with no comment to post and no instruction below to submit a review anyway, delete it instead (`gh api -X DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>`).
blocks.leaveReviews: Post your findings in that review, following the review-comment rules in my CLAUDE.md: one inline comment per finding, describe the problem and its concrete impact only (never propose the fix), strip every internal severity/category marking from the text, and never leave an LGTM / "no issues" comment. NEVER POST A DUPLICATE FINDING: before writing a single comment, read EVERY comment and review thread already on the PR — mine, other reviewers', earlier review runs', resolved or not. If an existing comment already mentions a bug you found, do NOT leave a second comment about it under any circumstances — reply on that existing thread instead ("Still present as of <commit_hash>", with the PR's actual current head commit hash). One issue = one thread, ever. A limitation the PR description acknowledges is NOT a resolved finding: if the code still produces a wrong result, report it.
blocks.noReviews: Do NOT post your findings on the PR — no inline comments, no thread replies, no top-level comments; report them to me in your summary instead. Only an instruction below that explicitly tells you to submit a review may post anything.
blocks.reply: For review threads that OTHERS have left on these PRs: address each one, and never mark a thread resolved without first replying "Fixed in <commit_hash>" with the real commit hash.
blocks.noVerdict: Do NOT submit an APPROVE or a REQUEST-CHANGES verdict — the final approve / changes-requested call is mine. Any review you submit on this PR uses the neutral COMMENT event, never APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES. If the PR comes back clean with nothing to post at any level, don't post an LGTM — delete any pending review you opened, and just tell me in your summary that PR #{pr} looks clean and is ready for my approval.
blocks.softApprove: Do NOT submit an APPROVE or a REQUEST-CHANGES verdict — the final approve / changes-requested call is mine; any review you submit on this PR uses the neutral COMMENT event, never APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES. The ONE deliberate exception to the no-LGTM rule: when a PR comes back PERFECTLY clean — no issues, regressions or bad practices left at ANY level after the full sweep, LOW findings included — submit a review anyway, with no inline comments and a short friendly BODY noting you ran the full E2E sweep and it returned completely clean, and thanking them for contributing. It goes through the review lifecycle above like any review — the pending review, submitted with `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>/events -f event=COMMENT -f body=<that text>` — and never as a top-level issue comment. That body must say what you actually ran and went through — the moves you covered, the reproductions you executed — never a bare impression like "looks correct" or "held up throughout". For example: "Ran the full sweep: claims vs code, nearest twin, non-happy paths, inputs, reachability, lifetime, plus mutation across the new branches and constants. Replayed the flow E2E on a booted sim. Returned clean. Thank you for contributing!". This is a SOFT approval: a COMMENT review carrying that body ONLY — it must NEVER carry an APPROVE action or any other review verdict.
blocks.trailer: Keep dispatching swarms until every PR you go through comes back clean — where CLEAN means a pass that surfaced no HIGH and no MEDIUM finding. A pass whose findings are all LOW (or nitpicks) COUNTS AS CLEAN: post the LOW ones, drop the nitpicks, and stop iterating on that PR. Only a HIGH or a MEDIUM keeps the loop alive.
blocks.noAttribution: No AI attribution anywhere in git/GitHub — commits authored as me, no Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with" taglines.
blocks.diplomatTag: Diplomat attribution tag — a REQUIRED exception to the no-attribution rule, for GitHub commentary only: every comment, inline review comment, review body, and review-thread reply you post as part of this task must begin with the exact prefix `\[[Diplomat](https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat){model}\]: `, copied character for character — the `\[` and `\]` are literal brackets, only the word Diplomat is a Markdown link (to https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat), anything after that link is plain text, and a colon and a space close it — followed by the text you would otherwise have written, so it renders as "[Diplomat{model}]: <your text>". This is the ONE sanctioned attribution; it applies to posted comment/review text ONLY and never changes commit messages, commit authorship, or the no-Co-Authored-By / no-"Generated with" git rules, which remain in force.
blocks.finalPass:
Then, one last FULL E2E pass on the real built binaries with a full swarm of code-analysis agents, sized within the limits in my CLAUDE.md. Provide super-concrete reproductions for any finding you manage to surface. Deliver a verdict on each PR:
• If it turns out perfect — confirm every previously-raised issue is resolved, and if so, APPROVE it.
• If only LOW findings are left — post them as inline comments and still APPROVE; nitpicks are dropped, never raised.
• If there are major blockers — leave the review as "changes requested".
The no-duplicate rule holds here too: an issue an existing comment already mentions gets a reply on that thread ("Still present as of <commit_hash>"), never a fresh comment.
